question: What new trading feature is the retirement of the older trading website version meant to make room for?

answer:
The retirement of the old EnronOnline website version is meant to make room for the Spreads product. That product lets customers transact in both underlying legs of a spread at the same time.

The source is a 2001-02-16 email from David Forster titled "EnronOnline Website Changes". It announced two changes effective the following Monday morning:
- A new release for internal users only, which should fix the freeze-up of floating windows some users had reported.
- The old version of EnronOnline, the one without the news and weather content, would no longer be available.

The email states the reason directly: "The old version will be retired to make way for new functionality such as the Spreads product, which will allow customers to simultaneously transact in both of the underlying legs of a spread simultaneously."

Some customers were still using the old version. The email told staff to explain that the new version is just as fast as the old one but has additional functionality, like floating windows, news and weather. Staff were also to transfer any confused customers to Product Control.

I ran two searches and found only this one email on the topic. I didn't open it in full, because the search result already contained the whole message.
